kicker: City gas distribution · EBITDA per unit of gas sold, Q2 FY27
title: City gas: unit profit ran from ₹10.8 to below zero
dek: Three of five city gas distributors earned less per unit of gas in Q2 than in Q1, as West Asia LNG cuts and changes to cheap domestic gas quotas raised gas costs. Brent's slide to $91.8 on 17 Nov eases oil-linked gas costs.

read: Gas sourcing and pricing, not demand, set Q2 unit profit: only ATGL, which raised CNG prices and locked in a term contract, earned more per unit than in Q1.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Brent: NewsBytes, 17 Nov 2026
notes: EBITDA per scm is Vantage's division of each company's call-stated quarterly EBITDA by gas volume sold (daily volumes × 91 days in Q1 and 92 in Q2); MGL uses EBITDA from operations and IRM EBITDA excluding other income, with IRM's Q1 volume taken as H1 less Q2 (its Q1 call cited 50.9 MMSCM, which does not reconcile), so IRM's Q1 figure (₹10.5) is above the 'about ₹10' it stated; Gujarat Energy's figures are its own city-gas segment numbers (its Q1 call gave ₹5.18 for Q1, the Q2 call ₹4.65), because its total includes gas trading. Year-on-year margin changes are from filed consolidated results; Gujarat Energy (the merged Gujarat Gas group, revenue +147.7%) is excluded from that comparison because the year-ago base is not comparable, and Adani Total Gas has no Q2 filing in our results data. Causes are as stated on the Q2 calls: term LNG curtailed under force majeure (Qatar), cuts and reallocation of cheaper domestic APM/HPHT gas, and spot LNG at $22–30+/MMBtu; IGL's spot share rose from 3% to 15% while ATGL cut spot from 15% to 7-8% through a long-term contract and raised CNG prices several times. News hook: Brent traded at $91.8 on 17 Nov 2026 (NewsBytes); part of term LNG and new domestic gas is priced off Brent, but spot LNG is not, so relief depends on spot cargoes too. A phased shift of HPHT gas allocation to consumption-based shares from November 2026 is expected by IGL and MGL to add domestic gas over the next year.
